facts: Lantern Tutors writes 30-minute lesson plans for volunteer tutors.
The learners are adults studying basic maths in the evening.
Plans must include a warm-up, one worked example, two practice questions, and a closing check.
The learners may be nervous about maths.
assumptions: Use simple, everyday contexts to reduce anxiety.
Keep calculations to easy whole-number percentages.
Tutor will explain one idea at a time and check understanding often.
risks: Adults may have mixed prior knowledge, so pacing may need adjustment.
Wording or context may confuse learners if examples are not familiar.
Time may be too short if extra reassurance or recap is needed.

output.title: 30-minute percentages lesson plan
output.body:
Warm-up: Ask what percent means in everyday life. Say: percent means “out of 100.” Use a familiar example: if 25 out of 100 people like tea, that is 25%. Reassure learners that percentages are just another way to name part of a whole.

Worked example: Find 10% of £50. Explain that 10% means one tenth. So 10% of £50 is £5. Then say 20% is two lots of 10%, so 20% of £50 is £10.

Practice questions: 1) Find 10% of £80. 2) Find 20% of £30. Give time to talk through each step.

Closing check: Ask: “What does percent mean?” and “How do you find 20% if you know 10%?” If needed, repeat that 10% is one tenth and 20% is two lots of 10%.

output.decisionQuestion: Should we keep the lesson focused on calculating 10% and 20%, or broaden it to include other common percentages like 5% and 50%?
options: Use a different set of easy percentages
